draft.title: Hypothetical VRAM Scaling: 2048 vs 8192 Context Lengths (Fixed Model/Hardware)
draft.body:
I'm exploring a hypothetical scenario concerning VRAM usage with varying context lengths in local LLMs. This is purely theoretical, with no actual measurements performed. The premise is that for a fixed model, runtime, and hardware setup, increasing the context length from 2048 tokens to 8192 tokens hypothetically increases VRAM consumption from 7 GB to 11 GB.

No performance metrics (tokens/sec) or output quality assessments were part of this hypothetical exercise. The focus is strictly on the memory footprint difference as context length scales. This thought experiment aims to understand the potential VRAM implications for users considering longer contexts. What are the primary factors contributing to this hypothetical memory increase, and are there common strategies to mitigate it within similar theoretical frameworks?
